topic: Why does déjà vu feel so real?

Here's What It Actually Is' 36; 'Why Your Brain Lies About Déjà Vu' 35; 'Déjà Vu: Your Brain's Favorite Lie' 35; 'Why Do We Get Déjà Vu?' 33; 'The Science Behind That Weird Feeling' 30; 'Why Déjà Vu Happens (It's Not What You Think)' 32. Thumbnails: A a person mid-step freezing with a shocked face and a ghostly repeated outline behind them (chosen, headline 'IT NEVER ACTUALLY HAPPENED'); B a brain with two switches, one lit, one dark; C a rewind icon over a doorway. Hooks: 'You walk into a room and think: haven't I done this exact thing before?' (chosen); 'Your brain just told you a memory that never happened.'; 'That eerie feeling has a name, and it isn't magic.'; 'Scientists still argue about this one.'; 'Sixty to seventy percent of people feel this. Have you?'. Facts and status: about 60-70% of people report experiencing déjà vu at least once in their life, PARTIALLY VERIFIED (estimates across sources range from about 60% to two-thirds; Live Science and Bustle both cite experts in this 60-70% band, one outlier source claims 97% and was rejected as low quality); the leading scientific explanation is a mismatch between a 'this feels familiar' signal from the parahippocampal/perirhinal cortex and the hippocampus's actual memory recall - the familiarity fires without a real matching memory behind it, PARTIALLY VERIFIED (BrainFacts/Howard Eichenbaum's familiarity-vs-recollection account; no single mechanism is established as definitive, which the script states plainly rather than overclaiming); reported déjà vu frequency decreases with age, PARTIALLY VERIFIED (cited in the same Live Science piece). Risks: avoid any claim linking déjà vu to epilepsy or implying it is a medical symptom - the script stays with the benign, universal experience only, never medical advice. scenes.text: You walk into a room and think: haven't I done this exact thing before?
That jolt is déjà vu, and here's the strange part: it isn't a real memory at all.
Your brain has a 'this feels familiar' switch, and sometimes it flips on by mistake.

graphic.headline: Quick chat
items: Why does this place feel so familiar?
Because one part of your brain says it's familiar.

scenes.text: Normally, feeling familiar and actually remembering happen together. In déjà vu, only the familiar switch fires.
About sixty to seventy percent of people feel this at some point in life. Ever had it?
No, it's not a past life. Your brain's 'familiar' alarm just tripped over its own wiring.

graphic.headline: Past life?
items: Myth: you saw this in a past life
Truth: your brain's alarm just tripped over itself

scenes.text: So that eerie feeling? Just a familiar alarm, firing a beat too early. Ever felt it? Tell me below, and follow to understand one new thing every day.

scenes.text: आप किसी कमरे में जाते हैं और सोचते हैं - क्या मैं पहले भी यहाँ आ चुका हूँ?
उस झटके को डेजा वू कहते हैं, और अजीब बात यह है - यह असली याद नहीं है।
दिमाग में एक 'पहचान' वाला स्विच है, और कभी-कभी वह गलती से ऑन हो जाता है।

items: ये जगह इतनी जानी-पहचानी क्यों लग रही है?
क्योंकि दिमाग का एक हिस्सा कहता है - पहचानी लगती है।
पर मैं तो कभी आया ही नहीं!

scenes.text: आमतौर पर पहचान और याद साथ आती हैं। डेजा वू में सिर्फ़ पहचान वाला स्विच चलता है।

graphic.headline: कहाँ गड़बड़ी होती है
items: पहचान वाला स्विच अकेला चलता है

scenes.text: करीब साठ से सत्तर प्रतिशत लोग जीवन में कभी न कभी यह महसूस करते हैं। आपको हुआ है?
नहीं, यह पिछला जन्म नहीं है। दिमाग का 'पहचान' अलार्म बस अपने ही तार में उलझ गया।

scenes.text: तो वह अजीब एहसास? बस एक अलार्म है, जो थोड़ा जल्दी बज गया। आपको कभी हुआ है? नीचे बताइए, और रोज़ एक नई चीज़ समझने के लिए फ़ॉलो करें।
